taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Market-road, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 104 | 2.86 | 2.86
2 | 186 | 2.38 | 5.24
3 | 266 | 24.7 | 29.9
4 | 327 | 24.6 | 54.6
5 | 219 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AAK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Market-road, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station Market-road, Bori Metropolis**

The VES interpretation at this station resolves five layers. Resistivity increases from 104 Ω·m (layer 1, 0–2.86 m) to 186 Ω·m (layer 2, 2.86–5.24 m) to 266 Ω·m (layer 3, 5.24–29.9 m) to a maximum of 327 Ω·m (layer 4, 29.9–54.6 m), then decreases to 219 Ω·m in the basal layer 5 (depth not resolved).

Applying the curve-type rule to successive triplets:
- Layers 1-2-3 (104<186<266): A
- Layers 2-3-4 (186<266<327): A
- Layers 3-4-5 (266<327>219): K

This gives curve type AAK, consistent with a steadily increasing resistivity trend through the upper four layers followed by a drop in resistivity at depth — typical of a resistive unit overlying a more conductive basement/aquifer zone.

The on-file classification (AAK) matches the computed curve type from the layer resistivity values; no discrepancy is found.

{"curve_type_stated": "AAK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
